title: Chapter 2 Quiz: Declarative Rendering & Directives
description: Test your knowledge of directives, conditional rendering, lists, class bindings, v-model, and advanced directives.

questions.question: Which directive is used to conditionally render an element and remove it from the DOM when false?
questions.explanation: `v-if` removes the element from the DOM when the condition is false. `v-show` only toggles visibility.

questions.question: `v-show` toggles the `visibility` CSS property.
questions.explanation: `v-show` toggles `display: none`. It doesn't affect `visibility`.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to provide a unique key for each item in a `v-for` loop?
options: It's optional, but using index is best
questions.explanation: A unique `id` property (or equivalent) is best for tracking each item. Using the index can cause issues when lists change.

questions.question: To bind a class conditionally, you use the _________ syntax with `:class`.
questions.explanation: Object syntax `:class="{ active: isActive }"` allows toggling classes based on boolean data properties.

questions.question: `v-model` provides two-way data binding for form inputs.
questions.explanation: Yes, `v-model` syncs the input value with a data property in both directions.

questions.question: Which directive would you use to render raw HTML?
questions.explanation: `v-html` sets the element's innerHTML to the provided string. Use with caution to avoid XSS.

questions.question: What is the shorthand for `v-on:click`?
questions.explanation: `@click` is the shorthand for `v-on:click`.

questions.question: You can use `v-for` with an object to iterate over its properties.
questions.explanation: Yes, `v-for="(value, key, index) in object"` works.

questions.question: The modifier that delays `v-model` updates until the `change` event is __________.
questions.explanation: `.lazy` makes `v-model` sync after the `change` event instead of after every `input` event.

questions.question: Which directive would you use to prevent an element from being re-rendered when its data changes?
questions.explanation: `v-once` renders the element only once and never updates it, regardless of data changes.

questions.question: `v-cloak` is used to hide uncompiled mustache tags until the Vue instance is ready.
questions.explanation: Yes, `v-cloak` stays on the element until mounting, often used with CSS `display: none` to avoid flicker.

questions.question: Which directive allows you to bind inline styles with an object?
questions.explanation: `v-bind:style` (or `:style`) accepts an object of CSS properties.

questions.question: The shorthand for `v-bind:href` is __________.
questions.explanation: `v-bind:` can be shortened to `:`.

questions.question: When using `v-if` with `v-else`, the elements must be adjacent in the template.
questions.explanation: Yes, `v-if` and `v-else` need to be used on sibling elements for proper functionality.

questions.question: Which modifier would you use with `v-model` to automatically trim whitespace?
questions.explanation: `.trim` strips leading/trailing whitespace from the input value.

questions.question: What does `v-pre` do?
options: Prevents the element from being compiled
questions.explanation: `v-pre` skips compilation for the element and its children, useful for raw mustache tags.

questions.question: You can use `v-for` and `v-if` together on the same element.
questions.explanation: Yes, but `v-if` has higher priority than `v-for` in Vue 2; in Vue 3, `v-if` has lower priority, which can affect performance. It's better to use a computed property or a wrapping element.

questions.question: To convert an input's value to a number with `v-model`, use the __________ modifier.
questions.explanation: `.number` attempts to convert the input value to a number.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid way to use `v-bind:class`?
questions.explanation: `v-bind:class` does not accept a function directly; it accepts an object, array, or string. However, you can use a computed property that returns the class string.

questions.question: `v-html` can lead to XSS attacks if used with untrusted content.
questions.explanation: Yes, because it injects raw HTML. Always sanitize user-provided content before using `v-html`.
